ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Eleven, soaring Dark Star and a fiery Lovelight
ai_show_review.blurb: The August 28 1968 Avalon set delivers a blistering The Eleven, a transcendent Dark Star, and a powerful Turn On Your Lovelight finish. Jerry’s guitar is “mach‑speed” on the Eleven and his solo on Lovelight shines. Despite muddy soundboard tape, the performance ranks among the band’s late‑summer highlights.
ai_show_review.review: On August 28, 1968 at San Francisco’s Avalon Ballroom the Dead rolled out a single set that still reverberates as one of the high points of that summer tour. The show bursts open with an incandescent Dark Star that showcases Jerry Garcia’s lyrical phrasing, then rockets into Saint Stephen before hitting the famously intense “The Eleven,” where Jerry and Phil lock in at what reviewers call “mach‑speed” intensity. A brief dip occurs on the solemn “Death Don't Have No Mercy,” but the band rebounds with a soaring Turn On Your Lovelight—Jerry’s solo here is cited as proof that his early‑’70s mythic status was already evident. The only real drawback is the soundboard source: both official tapes suffer from muddy, over‑processed EQ that muffles some of the nuance, yet they remain the sole complete capture of the set. For listeners seeking the full experience, the Cotsman SBD (gd68-08-28.sbd.cotsman.18104.sbeok.shnf) is still the best option despite its sonic flaws.

best_recording.reason: Only recording that captures the complete set; despite muddy EQ it provides the full performance, unlike audience tapes missing the first half.

key_highlights: Stellar Dark Star with soaring improvisation
"The Eleven" performed at breakneck, mach‑speed intensity
Jerry’s fiery solo on Turn On Your Lovelight
Overall high‑energy flow that defines August 1968

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers a beautiful Dark Star, flies through The Eleven at mach‑speed and adds a strong, memorable solo on Turn On Your Lovelight.
band_performance.Phil: Locks tightly behind Jerry during The Eleven, providing solid bass support throughout the set.
